title: Navigation is not reliably keyboard accessible
evidence: At a 1440px viewport, tabbing from the desktop About control moved to Sermons while its submenu remained display:none. Enter and Arrow Down did not expose its links. At 706px, the visible hamburger was a div with no role, accessible name or tabindex; Tab traversed off-canvas navigation while the menu remained closed.
reproduce: On desktop, use Tab to reach About, then try Enter, Arrow Down and Tab. At a narrow width, try to reach and operate the hamburger without a pointer. A developer can inspect #sp-header #nav_about and #sp-nav-button.
standard: WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard; 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; focus visibility needs remediation and retesting.
fix: Use real disclosure buttons with accessible names and expanded state. Support Enter/Space, sensible focus order and Escape. Remove closed off-canvas menus from keyboard and accessibility navigation.

title: Nine sermon thumbnail links have no descriptive accessible name
evidence: All nine image links under Previous Sermon Series had empty alt text, no link text, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby and no title. The accessibility tree exposed raw YouTube destinations instead of meaningful series names.
reproduce: Open Previous Sermon Series. Use a screen reader's links list, or inspect each thumbnail anchor and its image. The image-only anchors have alt="" and no replacement name.
standard: WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content; 2.4.4 Link Purpose; 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.
fix: Give every linked thumbnail a meaningful series or message title, preferably as visible linked text with an appropriate image alternative.

title: Footer text links have insufficient contrast
evidence: Contact Us, Journey in Redmond, Give Online and Watch Live use rgb(127,140,141), or #7f8c8d, against a white background. Calculated contrast is approximately 3.48:1. Text was 15px at 320px viewport and 16.5px in the desktop check, below the large-text threshold.
reproduce: Scroll to the footer. Measure #7f8c8d against #ffffff with a contrast checker; inspect the computed link color and size. The white background was checked visually, not inferred solely from ancestor styles.
fix: Darken the footer link color to a measured ratio of at least 4.5:1; also check hover and focus states.

status: Confirmed on all nine sampled main-site pages
title: Page language is not declared
evidence: Neither lang nor xml:lang was present on the document element on Home, Visit, Kids, Contact, Prayer, Care, Giving, Sermons or Media.
reproduce: Inspect the opening html element on any sampled page. document.documentElement.getAttribute('lang') returned null.
fix: Set the site's document language to English, such as lang="en", and identify passages in another language where needed.

title: Logo and social links lack meaningful accessible names
evidence: The logo anchor contains an image without alt text and no replacement name. Footer social anchors contain only icon-font elements, without accessible labels. The accessibility tree exposed a URL for the logo and icon glyphs for social destinations.
reproduce: Inspect #sp-logo a and footer .sp-social-holder a, or read their names with assistive technology.
fix: Name the logo link Journey Church — Home and label each social destination. Hide decorative icon glyphs from assistive technology.

title: Video and map frames lack descriptive titles
evidence: The YouTube frames on Home and Sermons, Google Maps frame on Visit, and Subsplash frame on Media have no title attribute. These are content frames; the finding excludes the many blank layout/resizer frames inserted by the platform.
reproduce: Inspect iframe[src] on Visit, Home, Sermons and Media. The actual content frames have source URLs but no descriptive title.
standard: WCAG frame-identification remediation; relevant to 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. Some embedded documents expose their own titles, which does not excuse omitting a clear frame label.
fix: Add concise titles such as Map to Journey Church in Bend and the actual sermon title. Check the resulting screen-reader frame list.

status: Confirmed missing explicit labels; assistive-technology retest needed
title: Media-library search relies on a placeholder
evidence: The library search input has placeholder="search..." with no label, aria-label or aria-labelledby. The category select also lacks an explicit label in the inspected markup. The search field appeared unnamed in the observed accessibility tree. Placeholder fallback differs between browser/assistive-technology combinations.
reproduce: Inspect the search input and category select in Media Library. Check the field's announcement on desktop and narrow layouts.
standard: WCAG 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions; verify 4.1.2 in the target browser/screen-reader combinations.
fix: Add visible, programmatically associated labels for Search messages and Browse by. Do not rely on placeholder text alone.

status: Public disclosure gap observed; legal applicability unresolved
title: Journey-specific privacy information was not found at the inspected collection points
evidence: No privacy/cookie notice links were found on the nine sampled main-site pages. The six inspected Church Center forms link to Planning Center's Privacy Policy; no Journey-specific notice covering its own handling was visible. The regular and urgent prayer forms do disclose sharing with prayer, staff and/or pastoral teams.
reproduce: Check the main-site footer, then the prayer form and its Privacy Policy destination. Look for Journey's purposes, retention, rights process and contact for privacy requests.
standard: If GDPR applies, assess Articles 12–14 transparency duties; a vendor policy alone does not establish that Journey's controller disclosures are complete.
fix: Publish a Journey-specific notice and link it where information is collected. State purposes, legal bases, recipients, retention criteria, rights and applicable transfers. Have Journey verify the actual practices before publication.
owner: Journey leadership / privacy owner with legal review

status: Sensitive collection confirmed; lawful basis and controls not observable
title: Hospital-visit form collects health and religious information
evidence: The form asks about hospitalization, allergies and whether the person follows Jesus, and collects a reason for hospitalization. Its wording permits information about another person. No Journey-specific sensitive-data notice or explanation of authority to provide another person's information was visible.
reproduce: Open Request a hospital visit and read the questions without entering any data. Check the introductory text and footer notice.
standard: If GDPR applies, evaluate Articles 5, 6, 9 and potentially 14. Religious nonprofit conditions in Article 9(2)(d) are limited, not a blanket exemption.
fix: Reduce collection to what is necessary for the visit; explain whose data is requested and why; establish authority and the applicable legal basis/Article 9 condition; restrict recipients and retention. A consent checkbox alone is not a complete solution.

status: Embeds and absent visible choice observed; tracking behavior unverified
title: Third-party embeds load without an observed consent choice
evidence: YouTube content loaded on Home/Sermons, Google Maps was directly embedded on Visit, and Subsplash loaded on Media. No consent banner or cookie-settings control was observed in this browser session. Exact cookies, storage writes, regional behavior and any prior browser consent were not established.
reproduce: Open Home, Visit and Media in a clean browser session. Use network/storage inspection from the relevant region before interaction, after rejection and after acceptance. This deeper trace remains required.
standard: Assess applicable EU ePrivacy rules and GDPR where personal data is processed. An embed or an absent banner alone does not prove unlawful tracking.
fix: Inventory actual storage and requests. Where consent is required, prevent nonessential loading until a valid choice, provide an equally easy refusal, and allow withdrawal. Offer a privacy-preserving video/map placeholder or external link as appropriate.

title: Newsletter signup needs clearer standalone information
evidence: The eScoop form shows its title, name/email fields, optional phone fields and a Submit button, without visible explanatory copy about email frequency, withdrawal or Journey's use of the information. The homepage describes the newsletter as weekly. No email was submitted, so unsubscribe handling was not tested.
reproduce: Open the signup form directly and assess what a person learns without visiting the homepage first.
standard: Transparency and purpose clarity; assess consent and applicable electronic-marketing rules. A separate checkbox is not automatically required for a dedicated signup form.
fix: Explain the newsletter and frequency, label the action clearly, link Journey's notice and explain unsubscribe. Remove optional phone collection unless there is a documented need; test unsubscribe and preference handling separately.

title: Connection card requires phone and address; child form collects family information
evidence: The connection card marks phone and address as required. The child-dedication form collects a child's name and age plus who will join on stage. Necessity, permissions, retention and access restrictions cannot be established from the public forms.
reproduce: Inspect the required fields on the connection card and the child-dedication form at /people/forms/396853. Do not submit test personal information.
standard: If GDPR applies, assess data minimization, lawful basis, child-data handling and retention. Collecting a child's data is not by itself proof that the GDPR's Article 8 online-consent rule applies.
fix: Document why each field is needed, make unnecessary fields optional or remove them, and explain child/parent data use. Confirm any separate photo/video permissions rather than assuming form submission grants them.
owner: Journey communications / kids lead + privacy owner
